paper.title: On the evolution of random graphs
paper.journal: Publ. Math. Inst. Hungar. Acad. Sci. 5:17-61

headline: Erdos-Renyi giant component (network generation): 3/3 locked clauses REPRO; frac(z=0.5)=0.0018, frac(z=2.0)=0.7991; matches S=1-e^(-zS) within 0.05 at z in [1.5, 2.0, 3.0]

verdicts.gate: P1 giant component absent below z=1, present above (frac(z=0.5)<0.05 AND frac(z=2.0)>0.4)
P2 sharp transition: fraction rises from <0.05 (z=0.5) to >0.40 (z=2.0) crossing z=1 (monotone non-decreasing)
P3 measured fraction at z in {1.5,2.0,3.0} within +/-0.05 of self-consistent S=1-e^{-zS}

extra.model_class: network-generation (NOT agent-stepping ABM): a static random graph is drawn and a structural property measured; no agents, scheduler, or ticks
extra.scope: faithful reproduction of a published synthetic network-science result; no real-world data; the contribution is whether the harness + discipline reproduce the giant-component phase transition and would catch an artifact

citations: Erdos, P. & Renyi, A. (1960). On the evolution of random graphs. Publ. Math. Inst. Hungar. Acad. Sci. 5:17-61.

benchmark.note: no cross-tool baseline; faithful single-implementation reproduction. Analytic anchor S=1-e^(-zS) serves as the theoretical baseline (P3).
